MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Geriatric Medicine Service Registrars & RMOs





Job no: 943628

Work type: Full time

Located in: Adelaide Metro Southern

Categories: Medical, Public Health




 

Southern Adelaide Local Health Network - Flinders Medical Centre - Rehabilitation, Aged & Palliative Care

Total Indicative Remuneration Package: $117,483 - $183,357 MDP2 (pro rata) 

Multiple Vacancies Available 

Build a Career That Matters - Service Geriatric Medicine Registrars & RMOs at Flinders Medical Centre

Full-time Service Geriatric Medicine Registrar and RMO roles at Flinders Medical Centre, Adelaide, until November 2029.

About the role: 

This role will provide clinical services of the highest possible standard to medicine patients of the Southern Adelaide Local Health Network (SALHN). In terms of individual performance and by contributing to a multi-disciplinary approach to the delivery of patient care. Duties for the role will include:

Provide a high-quality clinics servicer under the direction of the supervising consultant Physician.

Providing appropriate clinical care to patients.

Coordinating the follow up care of patients

Ensuring the maintenance of comprehensive clinical records which document significant patient management decisions

Ensuring effective communication with other care providers to promote continuity of patient care

Being responsive to complaints from patients and their relatives

Participating in the education of junior registrars, junior staff and students

About you:

Bachelor of Medicine; Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) or equivalent, registrable with the Medical Board of Australia as a Medical Practitioner with General registration (Geriatric Medicine); or another qualification as defined in the SA Medical Officers Award.

Ability to communicate effectively with a wide range of people including colleagues and other professional staff.

Good teaching skills.

Clinical experience and competence in the practice of medicine.

Ability to supervise more junior medical staff.

Ability to participate in continuing medical education activities.

Commitment to clinical audit.

Please see the attached Role Description for additional information.

The Queen's Club


Position  : Full Time 
Location : Sydney
Salary     : $75,000 - $85,000 a year 


A rare opportunity to join a long-established private Club in Sydney’s CBD. We are seeking an enthusiastic, professional Accommodation Manager to join our dynamic team in a full time capacity.

The role plays an important part in providing excellent service to our long-standing Members and their guests. The primary responsibility will be to ensure accommodation services operate efficiently and high standards of presentation of the rooms and Club are continually upheld. You will be an experienced leader with a dedication to exceptional operational standards and service delivery.

Key Duties
Oversee accommodation to ensure consistent operational excellence including being responsible for the day-to-day operations of the Reception, Housekeeping and Concierge team, anticipating and delivering on guest needs to achieve a high level of Member satisfaction.
Manage budgets to enable efficient daily operations.
Respond to Member enquiries in an efficient manner and resolve issues promptly and professionally
Monitor operational performance in housekeeping ensuring high service standards
Supervising housekeeping staff and contractors
Coordinate Reception and Housekeeping rosters
Provide ongoing staff training and recruitment in accordance with operational guidelines and SOPs
Establish and manage stock control systems, orders and supply processes
Ensure compliance with health, safety and hygiene standards
Prepare regular performance and operational reports
Maintain front office files and records as required
Support continuous improvement across accommodation operations
Ensure guest bookings are correct and confirm bookings. Checking accuracy of data and accounting entries for all transactions
Set up quality control measures and monitoring of all guest feedback
Attend Department Head meeting on weekly basis to report on reservations, property management and staff issues.

Key Attributes
Previous experience in accommodation operations and hospitality management or related services
Proven skills in staff management and leadership
Excellent customer service skills and communication skills (verbal and written).
Attention to detail and prompt attention to Members and Guests.
Highly organised and ability to work under pressure.
Providing friendly, personalised Member service in person or by phone.
Ability to use initiative to solve problems.
Fluent spoken and written English.
A high standard of personal presentation and grooming standards.
Excellent computer skills.
Must have a strong work ethic.
Flexibility in work hours.


If you meet the above criteria please apply now, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Targeted Vacancy       This is an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Identified role.  The program is designed to support greater representation of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples within the banking industry and is an equal opportunity measure under Section 105 of the Anti-Discrimination Act 1991. Only applications from Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people will be considered.     Launch Your Career as a First Nations Service Advisor Trainee - NAB Customer Call Centre    Start your career in personal banking at NAB's Melbourne CBD call centre! Join as a First Nations Service Advisor and complete a  12-month paid Business Traineeship  with MEGT while gaining hands-on experience.   What You'll Do?     As a First Nations Business Trainee in NAB's customer call centre, you will:    
 
 Deliver exceptional customer service via phone and digital channels 
 Handle transactions, resolve enquiries, and provide banking solutions within risk guidelines 
 Support customers with credit/debit cards, everyday banking, and self-service tools 
 Identify customer needs and refer to specialists when required 
 Accurately record customer interactions in NAB systems and CRM 
 Participate in team huddles, coaching sessions, and ongoing training 
 
  What We're Looking For?    
 
 Must be customer service focused with high computer literacy and strong customer service skills 
 Typing speed of 40-60 words per minute (desirable) 
 Strong communication skills and professional phone manner 
 Confident in a fast-paced call centre environment and able to multitask 
 Reliable, motivated, proactive team player with initiative 
 Identify as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander (essential) 
 Ability to pass a National Police Check (essential) 
 
   What's in it for You?    
 
 A full-time, paid traineeship with hands-on experience and learning 
 Ongoing coaching, mentoring and access to NAB's professional development resources 
 A pathway into a long-term career within the business and finance sector, with opportunities to move into roles such as Business Associate, Relationship Associate, or even Business Banker 
 Access to NAB's online learning portal and voluntary upskilling opportunities 
 A nationally recognised Certificate III in Business qualification 
 
  About NAB  National Australia Bank (NAB) is one of Australia's largest financial institutions, helping customers with personal, business and corporate banking needs. NAB is committed to delivering exceptional customer service, supporting local communities, and creating meaningful career pathways. As part of this traineeship, you'll be joining a business that values learning and growth.    Ready to launch your business/finance career?  Click  "Apply Now"  or visit  https://www.megt.com.au/jobs   At MEGT, we enable people to start their careers through Apprenticeships and Traineeships and support large and small businesses to recruit, train and grow careers. Our purpose is to provide life changing, lifelong learning and employment solutions for all. We invite you to be part of our story. Consent as an applicant to receive any marketing information related to other MEGT employment and education services offerings.  MEGT is committed to being a Child Safe Organisation and an Equal Opportunity Employer. We have zero tolerance of racism, discrimination, harm, or abuse. We have a culture that values safety, diversity, and inclusion and encourage all qualified applicants, including minorities, genders, protected veterans, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and individuals with disabilities are encouraged to apply.
